'''Shmuel Gal''' ({{langx|he|שמואל גל}}; born 1940) is a [[mathematician]] and professor of [[statistics]] at the [[University of Haifa]] in Israel.

He devised the [[Gal's accurate tables]] method for the computer evaluation of elementary functions.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last = Gal | first = Shmuel
 | editor1-last = Miranker | editor1-first = Willard L.
 | editor2-last = Toupin | editor2-first = Richard A.
 | contribution = Computing elementary functions: A new approach for achieving high accuracy and good performance
 | doi = 10.1007/3-540-16798-6_1
 | pages = 1–16
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science
 | title = Accurate Scientific Computations, Symposium, Bad Neuenahr, FRG, March 12–14, 1985, Proceedings
 | volume = 235
 | year = 1985}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=An accurate elementary mathematical library for the IEEE floating point standard |date=March 1991 |volume=17 |pages=26–45 |last1=Gal |first1=Shmuel  |last2=Bachelis |first2=Boris |journal=ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software |doi=10.1145/103147.103151|s2cid=16245519 |doi-access=free }}</ref>  With Zvi Yehudai he developed in 1993 a new algorithm for [[Sorting algorithm|sorting]] which is used by IBM.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://domino.watson.ibm.com/comm/wwwr_thinkresearch.nsf/pages/speeding396.html |title=Speeding of a sort |last1=Gwynne |first1=Peter |publisher=IBM Research}}</ref>

Gal has solved the [[Princess and monster game]]<ref name="Shmuel79">{{cite journal |author=Gal Shmuel |title=Search games with mobile and immobile hider |journal=SIAM J. Control Optim. |volume=17 |year=1979 |issue=1 |pages=99–122 |doi=10.1137/0317009 |mr=0516859}}</ref> and made several significant contributions to the area of [[search games]].<ref>{{cite book|first1=S. |last1=Gal |title=Search Games |publisher=Academic Press |location=New York |year=1980 |isbn=0-12-273850-0}}</ref><ref>S. Alpern and S. Gal (2003). ''The Theory of Search Games and Rendezvous'', Springer {{ISBN|0-7923-7468-1}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author=M. Chrobak |title=A princess swimming in the fog looking for a monster cow |journal=ACM SIGACT News |volume=35 |issue=2 |pages=74–78 |year=2004 |doi=10.1145/992287.992304|s2cid=8687739 }}</ref>

He has been working on [[rendezvous problem]]s with his collaborative colleagues [[Steve Alpern]], Vic Baston, and John Howard.<ref>S. Alpern and S. Gal (1995). Rendezvous Search on the Line with Distinguishable Players, SIAM J. Control and Optimization.</ref><ref>V. Baston and S. Gal (1998). Rendezvous on the line when the players' initial distance is given by an unknown probability distribution, SIAM J. Control and Optimization.</ref><ref>S. Alpern and S. Gal (2002). Searching for an Agent who may or may not Want to be Found, OPERATIONS RESEARCH.</ref><ref>S. Gal and J. Howard (2005). Rendezvous-evasion search in two boxes, OPERATIONS RESEARCH.</ref>

Gal received a Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. His thesis advisor was [[Aryeh Dvoretzky]].
